source_snapshot.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and Mezzanine Network Board 1 IO expander and FRU
source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Use the BMC I2C interface and MUX at 0x72 to select Mezzanine Network Board 1 port 1, then verify that the IO expander and FRU endpoints expected by PID 1114953 reply on the routed bus.
procedure_facts: Log into the BMC and scan bus 5 before routing.
Read the MUX state at address 0x72.
Write byte 0x02 to 0x72 to enable MUX port 1.
Scan bus 5 again and compare against devices in PID 1114953.
criteria_facts: The Criteria field contains only generic after-test collection and unexpected-log review; it does not list expected addresses or response values.
source_conflicts: The item calls the path BMC I2C-6 while commands use Linux adapter 5; this may be zero-based or platform mapping but is not documented.
The source spells `i2c detect` and `I2cget`, while standard i2c-tools commands are `i2cdetect` and `i2cget`.
The Criteria omits the PID 1114953 expected address list needed to judge replies.
missing_source_information: Signed mapping of BMC I2C-6 to the current Linux adapter and MUX 0x72.
PID 1114953 expected IO-expander/FRU addresses and allowed extra/missing-device rule.
Meaning of MUX byte 0x02, original-state restoration value and kernel-driver ownership.
Approved safe probe method/address range; timeout and bus-lock recovery.
Whether required photos are command screenshots or physical images.

original_test_intent.statement: Functionally verify BMC reachability to Mezzanine Network Board 1's IO expander and FRU through the specified I2C-6/MUX-port-1 path by comparing the post-route endpoint responses with PID 1114953 and restoring the original MUX state.
must_preserve: The I2C-6 logical hardware path and its mapped Linux adapter.
MUX address 0x72 and owner-confirmed port-1 selection semantics.
Both the before-route and after-route observations.
IO expander and FRU endpoint comparison against PID 1114953.
must_not_infer: That bus 5 equals I2C-6 without a platform map.
That byte 0x02 selects port 1 on every MUX or is the original/restoration value.
That a full `-q` scan is safe for every device on the bus.
That address presence proves electrical continuity, signal integrity or solder quality.
That physical probing, soldering or board inspection is required when the source procedure specifies only BMC transactions.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly identifies command spelling ambiguity, state-changing MUX risk, need for PID mapping and the limitation that address visibility cannot prove physical electrical integrity.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 invents qualified probing, soldering/continuity measurement and physical photos as the core acceptance even though the source defines a BMC bus-routing/reply procedure. That changes a functional connectivity check into a manual electrical-inspection test and overstates MANUAL ONLY.

related_records: Other I2C buses, mezzanines and MUX channels require their own adapter/address/endpoint maps and cannot supply PID 1114953 values.
applicable_history.precedence_application: The exact Procedure defines BMC transactions as the test method. The title does not authorize adding unmentioned physical probing; PID 1114953 remains the required platform truth for endpoints.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Reclassify from MANUAL ONLY to a gated hybrid. After the BMC adapter/MUX/endpoint map and safe probe method are supplied, an Agent can execute and compare the functional bus evidence; the owner must approve the MUX write and judge results. Physical continuity remains out of scope unless the source is separately revised.

conditions_present: Execution location, candidate adapter, MUX address/value, before/after structure, endpoint classes and external PID reference are present.
missing: Adapter-5/I2C-6 mapping, exact expected addresses, MUX semantics/ownership/original state, safe probe method, restoration, photo type, timeout and recovery.
provider: Board/BMC owner supplies PID 1114953 endpoint list, adapter map, MUX datasheet/register semantics and safe access policy.
Test owner defines allowed missing/extra responses, screenshot/photo evidence and pass/fail criteria.
Lab owner approves the BMC session, MUX write and recovery.
safe_read_only_work: Run `i2cdetect -l`, inspect `/sys/class/i2c-dev` and I2C sysfs topology to map adapter names and mux-created buses.
Record BMC/board/FRU identities, current device bindings, SEL/log baseline and current MUX state only through an owner-approved non-forced read.
Compare the signed endpoint list with existing sysfs device enumeration without probing unknown addresses.
prohibited_until_resolved: Forced `i2cget -f`, `-q` or full-range scan, direct MUX write, driver unbind, log clear, bus reset, power cycle, retry or PASS claim.
closure_evidence: Signed map proves I2C-6 corresponds to the selected adapter and MUX 0x72/port 1 controls the named board.
PID 1114953 supplies expected endpoint addresses and safe per-address probe/read method.
Original MUX state, approved 0x02 transition/restoration, timeout, recovery and result evidence are recorded.

revision_candidate.test_name: Verify BMC I2C-6 Connectivity to Mezzanine Network Board 1 IO Expander and FRU
revision_candidate.purpose: Select the approved MUX path from BMC I2C-6 to Mezzanine Network Board 1 and verify that the PID-defined IO expander and FRU endpoints respond on the correct routed bus, with no unexpected bus errors and with the original MUX state restored.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the board/BMC firmware, Linux I2C adapter mapping, MUX model/address 0x72, Mezzanine Network Board 1 revision and PID 1114953 endpoint map in the signed recipe. Execute from the BMC, not the host OS.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The single mapped BMC I2C-6 path through 0x72 port 1 to the named board's IO expander and FRU. Verify only PID-defined safe addresses and allowed companions; no other mux port, bus, board, physical continuity, signal-integrity or solder inspection is in scope. Treat 15/5 minutes as estimates.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Board/BMC/PID revisions; signed I2C-6-to-Linux-adapter map; MUX part/address/register and 0x02 semantics; kernel-driver ownership; original/restore state; PID 1114953 expected IO-expander/FRU addresses and allowed extras; approved i2c-tools version and safe probe/read operations; photo/screenshot rule; timeout; BMC access; MUX/bus recovery; authorization and evidence storage.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: From the BMC, capture identity, `i2cdetect -l`, sysfs adapter/mux topology, bindings, logs and original MUX state using the signed non-forced method. Use only the PID-approved address probe or targeted read for a before-route observation; do not use the source's misspelled command or `-q` unless explicitly approved. After approval, write the exact owner-confirmed port-1 value to 0x72 once, verify the MUX state, repeat only the safe PID-defined endpoint checks, and compare IO-expander/FRU responses and unexpected devices/errors. Restore the exact original MUX state and verify final endpoint/BMC health.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Adapter/MUX/endpoint mapping and safe operations resolved; BMC/board/FRU revisions match PID; dedicated maintenance window; no competing BMC service/driver owns an incompatible access path; stable bus/SEL baseline; console and bus/BMC recovery proven; each forced access, scan, MUX write and restoration explicitly authorized.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: BMC/board/mezzanine/FRU/PID identities; adapter and sysfs mux topology proving I2C-6 mapping; i2c-tools version; driver ownership; signed expected-address matrix; original MUX state; before-route safe endpoint results; approved write transcript and verified port-1 state; after-route IO-expander and FRU replies at expected addresses with allowed-extra/missing comparison; timestamps/exit codes; screenshot or photo type required by the owner; relevant BMC logs/SEL; exact restoration and final bus/device health; engineer disposition.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: PID 1114953 plus the signed board schematic/BMC adapter and MUX-port mapping. Pass requires both expected endpoint responses on the correct post-route path, no disallowed address or bus error, and verified restoration; it does not claim electrical continuity or signal integrity.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not assume bus numbering, execute misspelled commands, scan unknown/full ranges with SMBus quick-write, force access to driver-owned devices, write 0x02 without MUX proof, leave the route changed, unbind drivers, probe/solder hardware, expose BMC credentials, auto-loop/retry or infer physical continuity from address visibility. Stop on mapping/state mismatch, NACK/timeout, bus busy/lock, unexpected address, FRU/IO failure, BMC management impact or failed restoration.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Board/BMC owner approves adapter, endpoint, MUX and safe-probe semantics; lab owner approves maintenance window, BMC access, one MUX write and recovery; test owner approves expected-address and screenshot/photo rules. Engineer retains PASS/FAIL judgment and authorizes any bus recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: No physical manipulation is required by the source. After exact handoff, an Agent may collect BMC topology, execute one approved MUX transition, perform safe targeted checks, compare evidence and restore state. Humans provide protected access, mapping, approvals and exceptional bus/BMC recovery.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On wrong mapping/state, bus lock, device loss or BMC impact, stop new transactions, preserve outputs and restore only the recorded original MUX byte through the signed method. If restoration is unsafe or fails, use the board owner's bus/BMC recovery; prove management, IO-expander and FRU health before any rerun.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: PID/adapter/MUX/endpoint mapping or expected addresses unresolved; safe probe/read, original/restore state, approval, timeout or recovery missing; driver ownership conflicts; tool spelling/version differs; pre-state mismatches; MUX write/verification fails; expected endpoint missing, unexpected/disallowed address appears, bus locks/errors, BMC or FRU/IO behavior degrades; or restoration/final health fails.

identified_defects: V2 invents physical probing/soldering/continuity and makes it core acceptance without source support.
BMC I2C-6 versus Linux adapter 5 is undocumented.
Source command names/capitalization are invalid or ambiguous.
PID expected endpoints are absent from Criteria.
The source's `-q` scan and forced read can be unsafe, and MUX restoration is unspecified.
Generic photo language does not prove that physical photos rather than screenshots are required.
reason_for_change: Restore the source's functional BMC I2C routing/reply test, remove unrequested physical continuity work, and gate automation on the exact PID endpoint map plus safe MUX/probe semantics instead of declaring the case inherently manual.

new_technical_evidence.title: Implementing I2C Device Drivers in Userspace
new_technical_evidence.supports: Linux I2C adapter numbers must be mapped through sysfs or `i2cdetect -l`; userspace transfers act on the selected adapter and cannot establish board naming by number alone.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The platform-specific I2C-6-to-adapter-5 map is absent.

new_technical_evidence.title: Linux I2C Sysfs
new_technical_evidence.applicability: BMC kernel using Linux I2C mux topology
new_technical_evidence.supports: Sysfs device and `mux_device` links distinguish physical adapters from logical mux-created child buses, enabling a read-only topology proof before direct MUX access.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The exact BMC driver topology and whether direct 0x72 access is approved remain unknown.

new_technical_evidence.title: i2cdetect(8)
new_technical_evidence.supports: The command is `i2cdetect`; scanning issues arbitrary SMBus probes, can disrupt a bus, and `-q` quick-write probing is explicitly not recommended, supporting a signed safe-address method.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The BMC's exact i2c-tools build and device-specific safe probes must be confirmed.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-HW Robust-00005-V002
new_technical_evidence.supports: The BMC execution location, bus/MUX operations, PID reference, generic evidence request and timing.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Expected endpoints, safe commands, mapping, restoration and photo type are absent.

removed_ambiguities: Defines the test as functional bus reachability rather than physical continuity.
Requires proof of I2C-6-to-adapter mapping instead of assuming bus 5.
Replaces ambiguous full quick-write scanning with owner-approved safe endpoint checks.
Requires original MUX-state restoration and clarifies photo/screenshot evidence.
resolved_blockers: Physical probing and soldering are not source-required manual boundaries; after platform inputs and approval, command execution and evidence comparison are automatable.
remaining_blockers: Execution awaits PID endpoints, adapter/MUX mapping, safe probe/write semantics, evidence rule, approval and recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 removes a fabricated manual electrical test, preserves the actual BMC routing/reply intent, and adds the missing bus-map, scan-safety, endpoint-matrix and restoration controls needed for safe hybrid automation.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The contract-only validator understood a BMC-side functional routed-bus test, explicitly excluded physical continuity/probing, required both IO-expander and FRU responses and exact MUX restoration, and found the targeted-access/ownership/scan safety sufficient after platform handoff.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Reliability row 127 logs into the BMC, reads/writes MUX 0x72, scans adapter 5 before/after and references PID 1114953; it never instructs physical probing.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly catches command/MUX risks but transforms the source into a manual continuity/probing test and therefore overclassifies it as MANUAL ONLY.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow read-only adapter/sysfs/PID reconciliation now; permit one mapped MUX transition and safe endpoint comparison only after exact map, probe method, restoration, approval and recovery are signed.
